instructions: Squeeze 1 of the lemons. That should be about 2 tbsp of juice. Cut the other lemon into wedges.
Cut the 1.5 lb basa fillets into pieces about 2 inches long. Pat them dry with paper towels.

Grate the ginger and the 3 garlic cloves into a large bowl. Add the 1/2 cup besan, the turmeric, Kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, amchur and ajwain. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms over the bowl.
Stir in 1/4 cup of the yogurt, 1 tbsp of the lemon juice and 3/4 tsp of the salt. You want a thick paste that clings. If it's too stiff to coat the fish, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Add the fish and turn it gently with your hands until every piece is coated. Leave it for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the chutney. Pick about 1 cup of cilantro leaves and tender stems and 1/2 cup of mint leaves. Blend them with the last 1 tbsp lemon juice, the last 1/4 tsp salt and 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Stir the green paste into the last 1/2 cup yogurt in a small bowl.
Slice the red onion into thin rings.

Pour the oil into a large, deep skillet. It should be about 1 inch deep. Heat it over medium-high heat. You're heating it to 350°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Drop in a little of the paste: it's ready when it sizzles and floats up straight away without going dark.
Line a plate with paper towels. Lower in 4 or 5 pieces of fish, with room between them. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Fry them for about 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp.
Flip them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're deep golden all over and the fish flakes when you press it with a fork.
Transfer them to the lined plate and sprinkle them with some of the chaat masala while they're hot. Fry the rest the same way, letting the oil heat back up for a minute between batches.
Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve hot with the mint chutney, the onion rings and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: All three coat firm fish in a besan paste with ginger, garlic, ajwain, chili, turmeric and lemon, rest it 10 to 30 minutes and fry it until golden, finishing with chaat masala and lemon. Swasthi's Recipes (the lead) loosens the paste with curd and deep fries, or pan fries with dry-roasted besan; Fun Food Frolic grinds garlic, ajwain and coriander seed into the paste and uses king mackerel, and My Food Story adds a rice flour dusting and air fries. This follows the lead's deep-fry method with basa, a boneless white fish the sources name, keeps the chili to mild Kashmiri, and adds the mint and cilantro chutney the other two serve it with. Only the lead has 20 or more ratings.
